NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Platform and Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and cloud infrastructure engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing, building and operating reliable cloud platforms, maintaining infrastructure as code, and leading technical work across platform and product teams. Focused on self-service infrastructure, clear operational practices and observability that helps teams run services confidently.

EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd | April 2022–Present
- Tech lead for a five-person platform team; operate an AWS EKS platform spanning eight clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions.
- Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3; adopted by all 14 product teams and reduced time from new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Introduced SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error budget policies for the 20 most critical services; weekly on-call pages decreased by approximately 60%.
- Led migration from managed node groups to Karpenter and Spot instances for stateless workloads; reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established incident and post-mortem processes.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games | January 2019–March 2022
- Operated AWS game backend infrastructure for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players, using EC2, ECS and EKS.
- Managed AWS infrastructure in Terraform across approximately 40 modules and introduced Atlantis plan and apply workflows for pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability.
- Led launch capacity planning and used k6 load tests, including tests simulating 300,000 concurrent players; identified and resolved a connection pool limit before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting | July 2016–December 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021, renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

TECHNICAL SKILLS
AWS: EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront
Infrastructure as code and platform: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter
Observability and reliability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions, Puppet
Other: Linux, k6

ADDITIONAL CONTRIBUTIONS
- Speaker at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024: “SLOs that product managers care about”.
- Mentored three engineers moving from backend engineering into SRE.
- Built an open-source Kubernetes controller in Go to delete expired preview namespaces; approximately 120 GitHub stars.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including designing and operating AWS platforms, building reliable deployment paths for product teams, and leading technical work from proposal through production.

At Tallybrook, I am the tech lead for the platform team operating an EKS environment across eight clusters and three regions. I built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD and Crossplane, now adopted by all 14 product teams. This reduced the path from a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day. I also introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages by approximately 60%, and led a Karpenter and Spot migration that cut EC2 spend by 38%.

My earlier work at Brightwater Games included managing AWS infrastructure in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, introducing Atlantis workflows for pull requests, and improving observability with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki. I also led capacity planning and load testing for game launches. These experiences are relevant to Corvale's need for dependable cloud infrastructure, approachable infrastructure as code, and services that backend developers can monitor and operate effectively. I am used to leading technical topics and working with product teams to agree practical reliability policies.

The opportunity to help shape infrastructure for Corvale's new train fleet, from system design through production, is a compelling application of that platform and reliability experience. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute to the team.

Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz
